To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the NSA selects and expands a heterogeneous stem/pro-genitor cell population, (ii) rigorous clonal and subcloning analyses of NSCs are required to unequivocally document their stem cell activity, and (iii) cryopreserved neural stem cells retain their clonogenic and differentiation capacity.

the neurosphere assay can be used as a powerful tool to isolate, propagate, and characterize NSC cultures; however, the stemness and clonal properties of NSCs must be rigorously assessed by performing clonal and serial clonal analyses.
the NSA is a powerful method for the isolation and propagation of NSCs, and that clonal and serial clonal analyses are essential to detect, characterize, and unequivocally identify NSCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and in vitro characterization of NSCs.
the development and application of novel approaches for the in vitro propagation and cryopreservation, the clonal analysis, and the functional characterization of CNS stem cells.
the development of methods and protocols for the in vitro propagation and cryopreservation, as well as the clonal analyses of NSCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neurosphere assay can be used as a reliable tool for isolating and propagating NSCs, provided that the clonal analyses are performed to identify and document stem cell properties.
the clonal and serial clonal analyses of the neurosphere assay cultures are essential to unequivocally define and characterize the stem cell activity in the CNS.
, although the neurosphere assay has proven to be a useful method to enrich for NSCs, the identification and characterization of bona fide NSCs requires rigorous clonal analyses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NSA is an excellent tool for the initial isolation of stem cells, but the stem cell activity must be rigorously demonstrated through serial subcloning and clonal analysis.
clonogenic assays are a prerequisite for the identification and functional characterization of stem cells in vitro.
clonal and serially subcloned NSCs are capable of self-renewing in vitro and differentiating into neurons and glia, and can be cryopreserved and thawed without loss of their clonal properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NSA is not a clonal assay and that clonal analyses are essential for the identification of stem cells.
, although the majority of NSCs are capable of extensive self-renewal in vitro, only a subset of these cells can generate secondary neurosphere cultures.

the clonal and serial analysis of NSC cultures is essential to identify and characterize bona fide NSCs, to assess the purity and clonogenic potential of the stem/progenitor populations isolated from different CNS regions, and to evaluate the efficiency and reproducibility of the in vitro culture conditions used to propagate and maintain these cells.
